A company sells and services landscaping equipment.  
  
The company wants to calculate an item's sales unit price using a flat profit rate of 20 percent.  
  
You need to adjust the item's unit price.  
  
What are two possible ways to accomplish the goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create a sales job price list for the specific item.
Configure the unit price on the item card for the item.
Create a sales price list for the specific item.
Run the Adjust Item Costs/Prices batch job.
Configure the unit price by using the Suggest Item Price on Wksh feature.

questions.explanation:
The Adjust Item Costs/Prices batch job can apply an adjustment factor to the Unit Price field for selected items. Suggest Item Price on Wksh. can generate suggested item-price changes using an Adjustment Factor; the suggested changes must be implemented to update the prices. Both methods support a consistent 20 percent factor-based price adjustment.

**Learn more:** [Set up prices and discounts - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/dynamics365/business-central/across-prices-and-discounts) · [Report "Adjust Item Costs/Prices" - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/application/base-application/report/microsoft.inventory.item.adjust-item-costs-prices)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is deploying Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
The company must post monthly general-journal batches for purchase expenses incurred during the month. The posted entries must use unique, incrementing document numbers. The numbers must increase by one and remain sequential.  
  
You need to configure the system to satisfy these requirements.  
  
Which three actions should you perform, in sequence? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.

options.text: Create a Template Batch with Posting No. Series.
Configure a General Journal with Purchase Reason Code.
Configure a General Journal Template with Purchase Type.
Create a Template Batch with No. Series.

questions.explanation:
A Purchase-type general journal template provides the appropriate journal context for purchase-expense postings. A number series defines the consecutive numbering sequence, and assigning it as the batch’s Posting No. Series causes posted general-ledger entries to receive the next posting number. A regular batch No. Series instead controls document numbers on journal lines before posting; a reason code is only audit context.

**Learn more:** [Create number series - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/ui-create-number-series) · [Table "Gen. Journal Batch" - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/ja-jp/dynamics365/business-central/application/base-application/table/microsoft.finance.generalledger.journal.gen.-journal-batch)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
The finance team needs to dispose of a fixed asset.  
  
You need to recommend the process for posting the fixed-asset disposal.  
  
Which two actions should you recommend that the company perform? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create and post a fixed asset G/L journal.
Select a Tax Category when posting the sales invoice
Create and post a sales invoice.
Manually adjust the depreciation amount in the fixed asset card.
Use the Reverse Transactions function to cancel the fixed asset record.

questions.explanation:
A fixed asset can be disposed of by creating and posting a Fixed Asset G/L Journal with the FA Posting Type set to **Disposal**. When the asset is sold to a customer, creating and posting a sales invoice with the fixed asset records the sale proceeds and the disposal. A disposal posting records the disposal value and resulting gain or loss; it is not accomplished by manually changing depreciation or cancelling the asset record.

**Learn more:** [Dispose of or retire fixed assets - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/fa-how-dispose-retire)

You need to configure Dynamics 365 Business Central so it permits receiving item quantities that exceed the ordered quantity.  
  
Which two options can achieve this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Configure a maximum order quantity for the item
Configure a maximum inventory level for the item
Set up and select an over-receipt code in the item record
Set up and select an over-receipt code in the vendor record

questions.explanation:
An over-receipt code defines the tolerance by which a received quantity may exceed the ordered quantity. Assigning that code on either the Item Card or the Vendor Card enables over-receipts within the configured tolerance for the applicable item or vendor.\
\
**Learn more:** [Record purchases with purchase invoices - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/dynamics365/business-central/purchasing-how-record-purchases)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A large distribution company uses Business Central.  
  
The number of inventory transactions has tripled since implementation, and users encounter performance issues when posting transactions.  
  
You need to review Inventory Setup and update the configuration.  
  
Which configuration should you use?

options.text: Enable expected cost posting of G/L.
Enable cost adjustment logging for all transactions.
Configure automatic cost adjustment to never.
Configure automatic cost adjustment to always.

questions.explanation:
For a high-volume inventory operation, automatic cost adjustment during posting can degrade posting performance. Setting **Automatic Cost Adjustment** to **Never** prevents cost adjustments from running in the interactive posting process; the adjustments can be run later as a batch job or scheduled job queue task.

**Learn more:** [Set up general inventory information - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/inventory-how-setup-general) · [Schedule jobs for adjusting and reconciling inventory cost - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-adjust-reconcile-inventory-cost-job-queue)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A customer uses Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
The customer currently sends quotes and invoices through postal services. The customer wants to start emailing quotes and invoices directly from Business Central.  
  
You need to set up outbound email.  
  
Which two possible methods can achieve the goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Run the Set up your Business Inbox in Outlook assisted setup tool.
Run the Email setup assisted setup tool.
Run the Set up email logging assisted setup tool.

questions.explanation:
Business Central supports sending sales documents, including quotes and invoices, by email after an outbound email account is configured. The **Set Up Email** assisted setup guide can create the account, and the **Email Accounts** page provides the manual configuration path. Business Inbox in Outlook and email logging do not configure outbound document email delivery.

**Learn more:** [Set up email in Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/admin-how-setup-email) · [Send documents and emails](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/ui-how-send-documents-email)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are a functional consultant who is configuring items in Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
You are setting up multiple units of measure for an item whose base unit of measure is PCS and whose additional unit of measure is BOX. One BOX contains 20 PCS of the item.  
  
You need to specify the relationship between these units of measure.  
  
Which value should be entered on the **Item Units of Measure** page for this item?

options.text: For the BOX unit of measure, set the Qty. per Unit of Measure to 0.05.
For the BOX unit of measure, set the Qty. per Unit of Measure to 20.
For the PCS unit of measure, set the Qty. per Unit of Measure to 0.05.
For the PCS unit of measure, set the Qty. per Unit of Measure to 20.

questions.explanation:
For an alternate item unit of measure, **Qty. per Unit of Measure** is the number of base units that the alternate unit contains. Because one BOX contains 20 PCS, the BOX record must have a Qty. per Unit of Measure value of 20.

**Learn more:** [Set up item units of measure - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/dynamics365/business-central/inventory-how-setup-units-of-measure)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You create a test instance of Dynamics 365 Business Central and enter transactions for testing. You create a production company instance in the same Business Central environment.  
  
You need to copy the setup and master data from the test instance to the production instance without copying transaction data.  
  
Which two methods can achieve this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Use the Run Migration Now function from Cloud Migration Management
Create and export a configuration package from the source company. Next, import into the destination company
Use the Copy Data from Company function from the Configuration Worksheet page
Use the Copy function from the Companies page

questions.explanation:
A configuration package can include selected setup and master-data tables, be exported from one company, and be imported into another, so transaction tables can be excluded. The Configuration Worksheet also supports copying selected data from one company to another within the same tenant. In contrast, the Companies page Copy action creates a company from the source company’s contents, rather than selectively excluding transaction data.

**Learn more:** [Set up company configuration packages - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/administration/set-up-standard-company-configuration-packages) · [Migrate data to Business Central - Training](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/migrate-data-dynamics-365-business-central/)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central. The company has a customer that will also become a vendor for the company in the next financial year.  
  
The company intends to consolidate the customer and vendor balances to reduce unnecessary payments on receipts and lower transaction fees.  
  
You need to configure the contact card.  
  
Which option should you configure first?
questions.explanation:
To consolidate balances, the customer and vendor must be linked through the same company contact. Since the company is already set up as a customer and is now also becoming a vendor, use **Create as Vendor** on that contact to create and link the vendor record.

**Learn more:** [Consolidate Balances for a Company that is a Customer and a Vendor - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-consolidate-customer-vendor-balances)

questions.question:
The general ledger account for accounts receivable must equal the total of all balances on the customer cards.  
  
You need to configure the general ledger account card for accounts receivable to satisfy this requirement.  
  
What should you do?
questions.explanation:
Disable direct posting on the accounts receivable G/L control account. This prevents users from posting entries directly to that G/L account without creating corresponding customer ledger entries, so the G/L balance remains reconcilable to the total customer balance. Microsoft states that customer subledger balances can be reconciled to receivables G/L accounts when direct posting is disabled.\
\
**Learn more:** [Report overview - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/reports-available-reports)

questions.question:
The general ledger account for accounts receivable must equal the total of all balances on the customer cards.  
  
You need to configure the general ledger account card for accounts receivable to satisfy this requirement.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: The account cannot be used in any posting groups or posting setup
The account cannot be used in any account schedule.
The general ledger account cannot allow for direct posting.
The account must have ledger entries.

questions.explanation:
When **Check G/L Account Usage** is selected in General Ledger Setup, a G/L account must not be used in any posting groups or posting setup before it can be deleted. Microsoft Learn also specifies separate balance and ledger-entry-date requirements for account deletion.

**Learn more:** [Set up or change the chart of accounts - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-setup-chart-accounts)

Does this solution achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
The **Create FA Depreciation Books** batch job is used to assign a depreciation book to multiple fixed assets; it does not duplicate newly posted fixed-asset entries across books. Simultaneous entry creation in multiple depreciation books requires configuring depreciation-book entry duplication, such as adding the destination book to the duplication list.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set Up FA Depreciation - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/fa-how-setup-depreciation) · [Depreciation methods for fixed assets - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/fa-depreciation-methods)

questions.question:
Solution: Enable a duplication list to post to multiple depreciation books.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A duplication list duplicates fixed-asset journal lines into a separate journal for the other depreciation books, where the lines can be reviewed or changed and then posted. It does not itself post depreciation entries automatically to both books simultaneously.\
\
**Learn more:** [Depreciate or amortize fixed assets - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/fa-how-depreciate-amortize) · [Depreciation methods for fixed assets - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/fa-depreciation-methods)

questions.question:
Solution: Update the **FA Posting Type** setup.  
  
Does this solution fulfill the goal?
questions.explanation:
FA Posting Type Setup defines how posting types are handled for each depreciation book, such as their effect on book value and the depreciable basis. It does not duplicate depreciation postings to another book. Business Central uses a duplication list or a duplicate depreciation-book setting to create entries for different depreciation books.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set Up FA Depreciation - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/fa-how-setup-depreciation) · [Depreciate or amortize fixed assets - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/fa-how-depreciate-amortize)

questions.question:
Solution: Update the **FA Posting Type** setup.  
  
Does this solution fulfill the goal?
questions.explanation:
The goal is to post the same depreciation entry into more than one depreciation book. Using the duplication feature in the Fixed Asset G/L Journal accomplishes this: when the target book is flagged Part of Duplication List and the journal line specifies the duplicate depreciation book (Use Duplication List / Duplicate in Depreciation Book), Business Central automatically creates a matching entry in the second book when the line is posted. Because this is exactly the mechanism Business Central provides for posting to a second depreciation book, the solution does meet the goal (Yes). Both the automated key and the independent solver agree on Yes, consistent with the documented duplication-list behavior.

**Learn more:** [Depreciate or amortize fixed assets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/fa-how-depreciate-amortize)

The company requires that the acquisition cost be posted to the general ledger and that the salvage value be included in the fixed asset ledger entries.

What should you do?

Use purchase order to post the acquisition cost and salvage value at the same time.

questions.explanation:

## Background

Northwind Traders is an independent, family-owned business. The company distributes natural pet products in the Northwest region of the country/region. Products are bought directly from manufacturers and distributed using its own fleet of trucks.

When the company first started, deliveries were within a three-hour radius of the warehouse. Due to regional growth, current deliveries require drivers to stay overnight on some routes. The company plans to open a second warehouse to expand the region and eliminate overnights for route drivers. The company also plans to hire a second group of employees to run operations in this new location. The finance and accounting teams will remain in the original location.

The company uses a third-party system for financials and order management. The finance department stated that the company’s fiscal year begins on July 1 and ends on June 30. The mm/dd/yyyy date format is used.

As part of the expansion, the owner plans to upgrade to an ERP system and use Business Central to meet the company requirements and support growth.

## Current environment

### Orders
- Orders are emailed to customer service and manually entered into the inventory system.

### Pricing and discounts
- Customer pricing is determined by the customer market type. Customer market types are Retail, Veterinarian, and Breeder. Each customer is associated with only one market type.
- Vendors offer monthly promotions to customers by item, brand, or item category.
- Invoices should display each customer’s base price, the discount amount, and the net price.

### Accounts payable
- The company wants to expand vendor payment options in the new system.

## Requirement

### Customers
- The sales team must be able to do the following:
  - Quickly set up new customers with the proper settings based on customer type.
  - Identify customers by market type. Customer posting groups will be used to identify which market the customer belongs to.
- Base price is determined by the customer market type.
- The sales department should receive a warning when entering the order if a customer is over their credit limit.

### Sales
- Customer discounts are offered for specific time frames by item, brand, or product category. Discounts should be added to sales lines automatically.
- Discounts must post to a unique general ledger (G/L) account.
- The business needs to be able to track revenue by location, market, and product category dimensions. Locations 100 and 200 will be set as default dimensions on the two warehouse locations. Food, treats, toys, and supplies are the required product categories, which will be set as default dimensions on the item cards. Each customer card will have a default market dimension.
- The sales manager wants to delete canceled orders and automatically archive them.

### Warehouse
- Orders will be fulfilled from two possible warehouse locations.
- Product will be transferred between locations by using transfer orders.

### Sales invoices
- Invoices will be posted after delivery.
- Invoices will be emailed to the customer.
- The sales department must be able to quickly correct posted invoices for the following scenarios:
  - Posted invoices that have not been paid.
  - Posted invoices that have been paid.
  - Posted invoices created from sales orders.
  - Posted invoices not created from sales orders.

### Accounting
- The finance department requires that the company has 12 monthly accounting periods per fiscal year.
- Finance department users must be able to reconcile the accounts receivable (AR) subledger to the G/L account at month end.
- AR department users need the ability to settle and close invoices when customers take payment discounts after the payment discount date has passed. AR users should be allowed to accept or reject the payment tolerance.
- Accounts payable (AP) department users must be able to pay vendors by electronic funds transfer (EFT) and use a payment journal batch named EFT to process payments.
- When viewing G/L entries, the finance and accounting teams must be able to see debits and credits instead of a positive or negative amount.
- The company needs to be able to track expenses by department and location. The departments are sales, operations, and administration.
- AR must be able to correct cash application entries.

## Issues

### Payment application
- Customers may have several stores that are responsible for their own orders and payments.
- Occasionally, AR clerks mistakenly apply payments to the incorrect customer invoice.

### Invoicing
- When items are delivered, customers refuse the items for reasons such as damaged or wrong item.
- After the invoices are posted, they must be corrected, which is time-consuming.

### Warehouse
- The sales department and warehouse managers must have visibility into products that are in the process of being transferred between locations.

### Accounts
- Customer accounts are difficult to view by market type.
- The finance team does not have the ability to report revenue by customer type.

### Accounting
- AR users often find variances between the AR subledger and G/L account.
- Customers often take the payment discount after the payment discount date has passed, leaving open invoices for small amounts.
- The AP department is unable to pay vendors by EFT in the current system.
- Finance and accounting team members have trouble validating postings when they use only the amounts field on G/L entries.
- The finance department is unable to run financial reports by market. You need to configure Business Central so that G/L entries are displayed as required by the accounting team.  
  
Which configuration should you use?
questions.explanation:
The "Show Amounts" setting in General Ledger Setup controls how amounts are displayed on G/L entries and journals, letting you choose "Amount Only", "Debit/Credit Only", or "All Amounts". Because the accounting team wants entries presented a specific way (for example split into debit and credit columns), "Show Amounts" is the configuration you use, with "Debit/Credit Only" being the value you would select within it. "Debit/Credit" (option D) is a value/choice rather than the configuration setting itself, and "Check G/L Account Usage" and the G/L Account Card do not control the amount display mode. Therefore the correct configuration is Show Amounts.

**Learn more:** [Show Amounts in General Ledger Setup](https://yzhums.com/4985/) · [Understand the general ledger and Chart of Accounts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-general-ledger)

questions.explanation:

You must configure payment discounts to resolve the issue reported by the AR users.  
  
Which two options should you configure? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
A payment discount tolerance allows an invoice to be closed when a customer takes a discount after the payment discount date. The Payment Discount Grace Period defines the permitted late-discount window, and the Pmt. Disc. Tolerance Warning prompts AR users to accept or reject the late payment discount.\
\
**Learn more:** [Work with payment tolerances and payment discount tolerances](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/dynamics365/business-central/finance-payment-tolerance-and-payment-discount-tolerance)

questions.question:
You must configure payment discounts to resolve the issue reported by the AR users.  
  
Which two options should you configure? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Switch Blocked on the Customer Card to Yes.
Switch Direct Posting on the G/L Account Card to No.
Switch Blocked on the G/L Account Card to Yes.
Switch Direct Posting on the G/L Account Card to Yes.

questions.explanation:
Accounts receivable control accounts must receive postings through customer posting groups rather than direct G/L entries, so every G/L receivables entry corresponds to customer subledger activity. Setting **Direct Posting** to **No** on the G/L Account Card prevents direct entries that cause AR subledger-to-G/L variances. Microsoft states that customer subledger reconciliation assumes direct posting is disabled.

**Learn more:** [Report overview - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-au/dynamics365/business-central/reports-available-reports) · [Posting group setup - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-au/dynamics365/business-central/finance-posting-groups)

questions.question:
You need to set up a third location so that transfer orders can be posted between the two warehouses.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
A temporary transit location used by transfer orders must be designated with **Use as In-Transit**. This supports shipping inventory out of the source warehouse and receiving it into the destination warehouse while retaining visibility of inventory in transit.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set up a location card and define transfer routes - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/inventory-how-setup-locations) · [Transfer inventory between locations - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-nz/dynamics365/business-central/inventory-how-transfer-between-locations)

questions.question:
A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
A customer asks the company to always use its preferred shipping provider for every sales order.  
  
You need to configure the system to satisfy this requirement.  
  
What should you do?
questions.explanation:
A shipping agent represents the shipping company used to deliver items to a customer. Configuring the shipping agent enables it to be selected as the customer's shipping provider and used on the customer's sales orders.\
\
**Learn more:** [Table \"Customer\" | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/de-at/dynamics365/business-central/application/base-application/table/microsoft.sales.customer.customer) · [Set Up Shipping Agents | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/sales-how-to-set-up-shipping-agents)

questions.question:
A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
A customer asks the company to always use its preferred shipping provider for every sales order.  
  
You need to configure the system to satisfy this requirement.  
  
What should you do?
questions.explanation:
Over-receipt codes define the percentage by which a received quantity may exceed the ordered quantity. Assigning the applicable code on the Item card enables that tolerance for the purchased item. Microsoft Learn documents creating over-receipt codes and assigning them to items through the Item Card.

**Learn more:** [Record purchases with purchase invoices - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/dynamics365/business-central/purchasing-how-record-purchases)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Excel file containing journal entry data that must be imported into Dynamics 365 Business Central. The file was previously imported into a General Journal batch.  
  
You receive an updated version of the file that contains corrections, deletions, and new journal entries.  
  
Which two actions can you perform by using the Edit in Excel feature? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Modify an existing line in a General Journal batch
Insert a new line in a General Journal batch
Post one or more lines in a General Journal batch
Request Approval for one or more lines in a General Journal batch
Delete an existing line from a General Journal batch

questions.explanation:
Edit in Excel allows changes to existing General Journal batch records to be made in Excel and published back to Business Central. This supports updating an existing journal line and removing an existing journal line; posting and approval workflow actions are performed in Business Central rather than through the Excel editing integration.

**Learn more:** [View and edit in Excel from Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/across-work-with-excel)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses the average-costing method and inventory periods. Automatic Cost Posting is disabled.  
  
You close the inventory period for July 2020 and set the **Allow Posting From** field in General Ledger Setup to August 1, 2020.  
  
On August 8, 2020, you receive and post a purchase invoice for freight charges against a purchase invoice posted on July 15, 2020. You run the **Adjust Cost - Item Entries** batch job for August.  
  
You need to identify the adjustment entry associated with July after the batch job runs.  
  
Which date does the batch job automatically select for the value entry?
questions.explanation:
When an adjustment applies to a value entry dated before the allowed posting range, the Adjust Cost - Item Entries batch job assigns the adjustment value entry the date in General Ledger Setup’s **Allow Posting From** field. With July closed and the allowed date beginning August 1, 2020, the July-related adjustment is dated August 1, 2020.

**Learn more:** [Posting date on adjustment value entry compared to the source entry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/design-details-inventory-adjustment-value-entry-source-entry)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are deploying Dynamics 365 Business Central for a company.  
  
The company frequently places multiple shipments on a single invoice. You must train the accounting staff to process these sales invoices.  
  
Which two methods should you teach the staff for creating invoices? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Use the Combine Shipments batch job to automatically create and post sales invoices and credit memos.
Create a new invoice for the Bill-to-Customer. Use the Get Shipment Lines action to select all the shipments from different sales orders and Sell-to-Customers.
Use the Combine Shipments batch job to automatically create sales invoices and delete completed sales orders.
Create a new invoice for the Sell-to Customer. Use the Get Shipment Lines action to select all the shipments from different sales orders, in the same currency.
Use the Combine Shipments batch job to automatically create, post, and print sales invoices.

questions.explanation:
Business Central can manually combine posted, uninvoiced shipment lines by creating a sales invoice for the Sell-to Customer and using **Get Shipment Lines**; the shipments must be for the same customer and currency. It can also automatically create combined invoices through the **Combine Shipments** batch job, with options to post and print the invoices. Credit memos and deletion of completed sales orders are not functions of that batch job.

**Learn more:** [Combine shipments on a single invoice - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/dynamics365/business-central/sales-how-to-combine-shipments-on-a-single-invoice)

questions.question:
Solution: Define invoice posting policies on the **User Setup** page.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Invoice posting policies control a user's invoice-posting options, such as whether invoices may be posted with receipts or shipments. They do not define the default Type for purchase document lines. The purchase line default type is obtained from the purchase setup, so configuring invoice posting policies does not meet the requirement.\
\
**Learn more:** [Define an invoice posting policy for users - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/dynamics365/business-central/admin-setup-invoice-posting-policy) · [Purchase Line table - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/application/base-application/table/microsoft.purchases.document.purchase-line)

questions.question:
Solution: On the **Report Selection - Purchase** page, choose a purchase order document type, and then choose a custom report.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
The **Report Selection - Purchase** page configures reports and layouts used to print or send purchase documents. It does not control the default **Type** value on purchase order lines, so selecting a purchase order document type and a custom report cannot automatically populate that field.\
\
**Learn more:** [Report selection for documents in Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/across-report-selections)

questions.question:
Solution: On the **Vendor Card** page, choose a document layout, and then choose a custom report layout for reports.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Vendor document layouts control the report layouts used when documents are sent to vendors; they do not set or default the Type field on purchase order lines. Consequently, this configuration cannot automatically populate that field. [Define document layouts for customers and vendors](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-au/dynamics365/business-central/ui-define-customer-vendor-document-layouts)\
\
**Learn more:** [Define document layouts for customers and vendors](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-au/dynamics365/business-central/ui-define-customer-vendor-document-layouts)

questions.question:
Solution: On the Purchases & Payables Setup page, set the default document line type to **Item**.  
  
Does this solution achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Purchase Line `GetDefaultLineType` behavior uses the document default line type from Purchases & Payables Setup when it has a value. Configuring it as **Item** automatically initializes new purchase-order document lines with Type set to Item.\
\
**Learn more:** [Purchase Line table — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/de-de/dynamics365/business-central/application/base-application/table/microsoft.purchases.document.purchase-line) · [Purchases & Payables Setup table — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/ga-ie/dynamics365/business-central/application/base-application/table/microsoft.purchases.setup.purchases-%26-payables-setup)

questions.question:
Solution: On the Purchases & Payables Setup page, set the default document line type to **Item**.  
  
Does this solution achieve the goal?

options.text: Set the vendor's Priority field to 0 and create a workflow for generating vendor payments.
Set the vendor's Priority field to 1 and enable the Late Payment Predictions extension.
Set the vendor's Priority field to 1 and run the Suggest Vendor Payments process.
Set the Application Method to Apply to Oldest and run the Suggest Vendor Payments process.
Set the vendor's Priority field to 0 and run the Suggest Vendor Payments process.

questions.explanation:
In Business Central, priority 1 is the highest vendor priority because the lowest priority number other than 0 has the highest precedence. The Suggest Vendor Payments process uses vendor priorities to generate payment suggestions, helping ensure that this strategically important vendor’s payments are selected and processed on time.

**Learn more:** [Assign a priority level to a vendor - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/purchasing-how-prioritize-vendors) · [Suggest vendor payments - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/dynamics365/business-central/payables-how-suggest-vendor-payments)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are configuring a new company for a customer.  
  
The customer wants to sell items in boxes and pallets, while referring to the items as pieces. Each box contains 12 pieces. Each pallet contains 144 pieces.  
  
You need to assign units of measure to the items.  
  
How should you assign the units of measure?

options.text: Create Pieces as an item unit of measure with a quantity per unit of measure set to 1.

Create Pieces as a base unit of measure. Add Box as an item unit of measure with the quantity per unit set to 12.

With Pieces as the base unit, an alternate Box unit correctly has a quantity per unit of measure of 12 because each box contains 12 pieces. You need to create new customers.

**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: On the Contacts page, select Related Information and then select Customer.
On the Contacts page, select Create as Customer.
On the Configuration Template Header for the customer table, select Create Instance.

On the Customer card, select Apply Template.

Business Central can register a new customer from the Customers page by selecting New, or convert a selected contact to a customer through Create as > Customer. A configuration template for the Customer table can also create a new record through Create Instance. The Related Information customer action is for viewing a contact’s related customer, while Apply Template is used on existing customer records.

questions.question:
A company uses Business Central.  
  
A finance manager needs to ensure compliance with accounting standards by accurately recording financial transactions according to the document date and the posting date.  
  
You need to configure the system to synchronize document dates with posting dates on purchase documents.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Enable **Link Doc. Date to Posting Date** on the **Purchases & Payables Setup** page. This setting automatically updates the document date to match the posting date on purchase documents, supporting accurate accounting-date recording.\
\
**Learn more:** [Update document dates with posting dates - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/dynamics365/business-central/across-link-doc-dates-to-posting-dates)

questions.question:
A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
A customer wants to sell items that are not typically counted in the company's warehouse.  
  
You need to configure the system to fulfill this requirement.  
  
What should you set up?
questions.explanation:
The **Non-Inventory** item type can be used on sales documents but does not support inventory quantity, value, physical-counting, or warehousing processes. It is therefore appropriate for products that are sold without being managed as warehouse inventory.\
\
**Learn more:** [Understand item types - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/inventory-about-item-types)

questions.question:
A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
A customer wants to sell items that are not typically counted in the company's warehouse.  
  
You need to configure the system to fulfill this requirement.  
  
What should you set up?
questions.explanation:
Inventory Posting Groups determine the inventory balance-sheet accounts used for inventory postings. General Product Posting Groups classify items for general posting and, together with General Business Posting Groups in General Posting Setup, determine the relevant product cost and cost-of-goods-sold accounts.

**Learn more:** [Posting group setup - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-posting-groups) · [Design Details: Reconciliation with the General Ledger - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/design-details-reconciliation-with-the-general-ledger)

questions.question:
Solution: Create a new recurring sales line code. Then run the **Create Recurring Invoices** batch to generate the invoice.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Create Recurring Sales Invoices batch job creates invoices from recurring sales lines that have been assigned to customers and whose valid-from and valid-to dates include the posting date. A recurring sales line code must therefore also be assigned to the applicable customers; merely creating the code and running the batch is insufficient.\
\
**Learn more:** [Standard recurring sales lines - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/dynamics365/business-central/sales-how-work-standard-lines) · [Work with recurring revenue - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/dynamics365/business-central/finance-recurring-invoicing)

questions.question:
Solution: Create a sales quote for every customer. Add the sales lines to that quote. Then use the **Copy Document** feature to create a new invoice.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Recurring sales lines can be assigned to customers and used by the **Create Recurring Sales Invoices** batch job to generate sales invoices from the assigned standard lines. Creating and copying individual sales quotes does not establish recurring sales lines or provide the recurring-invoice system required for monthly subscription invoices.\
\
**Learn more:** [Standard recurring sales lines - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/sales-how-work-standard-lines) · [Work with recurring revenue in Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-recurring-invoicing)

questions.question:
Solution: Create a blanket order and add the required lines to it. Create the monthly sales order, and then create the invoice.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Blanket sales orders support long-term agreements and conversion of shipment lines to sales orders; they are not the feature for configuring reusable recurring sales lines. Recurring Sales Lines are the Business Central feature that defines standard sales lines for recurring sales documents and recurring invoice creation.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create recurring sales](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/dynamics365/business-central/sales-how-work-standard-lines) · [Work with blanket sales orders or blanket purchase orders](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/sales-how-to-create-blanket-sales-orders)

questions.question:
Solution: Create a new recurring sales line. Open the applicable customers and assign the Recurring Sales Lines code to each customer. Then run the Create Recurring Sales Invoices batch job to generate the invoices.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Business Central can create sales invoices through the Create Recurring Sales Invoices batch job using recurring sales lines assigned to customers. Assigning the recurring-sales-line code to the relevant customers provides the standard lines that the batch job uses to create their recurring invoices.\
\
**Learn more:** [Standard recurring sales lines - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/dynamics365/business-central/sales-how-work-standard-lines)

questions.question:

The company must be able to assign transactions unique, sequential numbers. Some transactions need multiple number series that can be used interchangeably.  
  
You need to configure number series to satisfy these requirements.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Define number series codes on journal templates.

questions.explanation:
Number series relationships associate multiple number series for the same type of transaction, allowing selection among the related series while each series supplies its sequential identifiers.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create number series - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/ui-create-number-series)

questions.question:
A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
You need to make sure that sales invoice discounts are calculated automatically.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: Discount Posting setting on the Sales & Receivables Setup page
Calc. Inv. Discount setting on the Sales & Receivables Setup page
Calc. Inv. Discount setting on the Purchase & Payables Setup page
Show Amounts setting on the General Ledger Setup page

questions.explanation:
The **Calc. Inv. Discount** setting on the **Sales & Receivables Setup** page enables automatic calculation of invoice discount amounts for sales documents, using eligible sales lines.\
\
**Learn more:** [Invoice sales - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/sales-how-invoice-sales) · [Sales & Receivables Setup table](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/application/base-application/table/microsoft.sales.setup.sales-%26-receivables-setup)

questions.question:
A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
You need to make sure that sales invoice discounts are calculated automatically.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: Set Email to Yes (Use Default Settings).
Allow Sender Substitution for SMTP Mail Setup.
Set Email to Yes (Prompt for Settings).
Assign a Document Sending Profile to the Customer where Email is set to No.
Apply Office Server Settings to the SMTP Mail Setup.
Assign a Document Sending Profile to the Customer where Email is set to Yes.

questions.explanation: To enable automatic emailing of invoices, the SMTP Mail Setup must have Email set to Yes (Use Default Settings) so outgoing mail uses the preconfigured server without requiring manual prompts, and the SMTP Mail Setup should be configured by applying the Office/Exchange server settings so the correct mail server connection and authentication values are used. In addition, the customer record must have a Document Sending Profile assigned with Email set to Yes so that posted documents such as invoices are routed to be sent by email rather than print or another method. Together, these three settings ensure invoices are sent via email automatically and correctly.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are configuring Business Central for a company.  
  
The accounting manager requires the following configuration for posted transactions:  
  
- Locations must be required for all users.  
- Bins must be required for every location.  
  
You need to configure the system to satisfy these requirements.  
  
Which two pages should you use? Each correct answer forms part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
The Inventory Setup page contains the Locations Mandatory setting, which requires a location code for inventory transactions. The Location Card contains the per-location Bin Mandatory setting, which enables and requires bin use for that location. [Microsoft Learn: Setting up inventory](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/inventory-setup-inventory) [Microsoft Learn: Set up locations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/dynamics365/business-central/inventory-how-setup-locations)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are deploying Dynamics 365 Business Central for a customer.  
  
You need to explain the primary functions of the Adjust Cost `" Item Entries batch job.  
  
What are the three primary purposes of the Adjust Cost `" Item Entries batch job? Each correct answer represents part of the complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Establish the earliest possible posting date for the Post Inventory to G/L process.
Calculate the correct cost of the sale of an item, according to an item's costing method.
Update the cost of goods sold (COGS) for historic sales entries.

questions.explanation:
Cost adjustment forwards cost changes from source entries to recipient entries according to the item’s costing method, ensuring correct inventory valuation and the correct cost of a sale. It updates COGS for historic sales entries when their applied inbound costs change. The batch job also validates and assigns the earliest allowed posting date to adjustment value entries, based on inventory periods and General Ledger posting-date settings, supporting subsequent inventory-cost posting to the general ledger.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A manufacturer uses Dynamics 365 Business Central to purchase items.  
  
When the manufacturer modifies or deletes purchase orders and blanket purchase orders, a record of those document changes must be maintained automatically. The configuration must not affect performance.  
  
You need to configure Business Central to automatically record these changes.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer is part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Open the Sales & Receivables Setup page.
Open the Purchases & Payables Setup page.

questions.explanation:
Business Central automatic document archiving creates a new archived version when a document is changed in relevant ways or deleted. For purchase documents, archiving is configured on the Purchases & Payables Setup page. Enabling archiving for orders and blanket orders preserves the required records without enabling change-log tracking.

**Learn more:** [Archive documents — Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-nz/dynamics365/business-central/across-how-to-archive-documents)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A heavy-equipment dealership is implementing Business Central.  
  
The client has the following requirements:  
  
- Track accounts receivable for parts and equipment sales in separate G/L accounts.  
- Track interest for parts and equipment sales in separate G/L accounts.  
- Use the same customer card for both parts and equipment sales.  
  
You enable the **Allow multiple posting groups** toggle on the Sales & Receivables Setup page.  
  
You need to define alternative posting groups.  
  
Where should you define the alternative posting groups?
questions.explanation:
Customer posting groups define the G/L accounts used for accounts-receivable transactions, including interest. After enabling multiple posting groups for sales, allowed substitute groups are configured by using the Alternative Groups action on the Customer Posting Groups page.

**Learn more:** [Set up posting groups - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-posting-groups)

questions.question:
A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
When users create sales documents, the system must show an alert with the customer's remaining credit. The alert must also notify the user when the customer has overdue payments.  
  
You need to set up a credit-limit and overdue-payment warning.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure the Late Payment Predict extension.
Select Both Warnings in the Credit Warnings field.
Enable the Exact Cost Reversing Mandatory field.

questions.explanation:

questions.explanation:

options.text: Assign a User Group to the user. Assign the Profile to the User Group.

Assign the Profile on the User card.
Add the user to the Profile card.

questions.explanation:
In Business Central a profile (role) can be applied to users in several ways: by assigning it on the User Personalization page (B), by marking a profile with the "Use as default profile" setting so it applies to users with no explicit assignment (D), and via user group membership where the profile is tied to the group (A). Assigning a profile directly on a "User card" (C) and adding a user from the Profile card (E) are not supported paths for user-level profile assignment, so they are excluded. This matches the accepted exam key of A, B, D.

The customer plans to sell items in D, but call the items **pieces**. Each box contains 12 pieces. Each pallet contains 144 pieces.  
  
You need to assign units of measure to the items.  
  
How should you assign the units of measure?

options.text: Create Box as a base unit of measure. Add Pieces as an item unit of measure with the quantity per unit set to 0.08333.
Create Pieces as an item unit of measure with a quantity per unit of measure set to 1.
Create Pieces as a base unit of measure. Add Box as an item unit of measure with the quantity per unit set to 12.
Create Pallet as a base unit of measure. Add Pallet as an item unit of measure with the quantity per unit set to 12.

questions.explanation:
In Business Central, an item's base unit of measure is the unit in which inventory is stored and is the conversion basis for alternate units. The alternate unit's quantity per unit of measure specifies how many base units it contains. Therefore, Pieces is the base unit, and Box is an alternate item unit containing 12 Pieces.

**Learn more:** [Set up item units of measure - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/dynamics365/business-central/inventory-how-setup-units-of-measure)

questions.question:
You are setting up payment terms.  
  
A company processes its standard vendor payments on the seventh day of the following month.  
  
You need to configure payment terms for the vendor.  
  
Which date formula should you use?
questions.explanation:
In Business Central date formulas, `CM` means the current month’s last day. `CM+7D` therefore calculates seven days after that month-end, which is the seventh day of the next month. Payment terms use such date formulas to calculate due dates.\
\
**Learn more:** [Entering dates and times in Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/dynamics365/business-central/ui-enter-date-ranges) · [Set up payment terms](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/dynamics365/business-central/finance-payment-terms)

You need to assign the units of measure to the items.  
  
How should you assign the units of measure?

options.text: Create Pieces as a base unit of measure. Add Pallet as an item unit of measure with the quantity per unit set to 144.
Create Pieces as an item unit of measure with a quantity per unit of measure set to 1.
Create Box as a base unit of measure. Add Pallet as an item unit of measure with the quantity per unit set to 12.
Create Pallet as a base unit of measure. Add Box as an item unit of measure with the quantity per unit set to 0.08333.

questions.explanation:
The base unit of measure defines the inventory unit and the basis for conversions to alternate units. Pieces must therefore be the base unit. An alternate Pallet unit must have a quantity per unit of measure of 144 because each pallet contains 144 pieces. A Box unit can similarly be added with a quantity of 12 pieces.

What is the result of the user's permission configuration?

options.text: The Yes option will allow a user to create a new customer.
The permission set order will allow a user to create a new customer.
The Blank option will allow a user to create a new customer.

questions.explanation:
Business Central calculates a user's effective permissions from the permissions granted through assigned permission sets. For an included permission, **Yes** grants the action, whereas **Blank** does not grant that action; it does not negate a grant from another assigned permission set. The user therefore has permission to insert Customer table records and can create a new customer.

A global trading company stores customer-information records in Business Central. The company regularly conducts international trade and works with customers operating in different currencies.  
  
You need to configure the system to invoice customers who use a foreign currency.  
  
Which two areas should you configure? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
A foreign-currency customer is configured with a default currency code on the Customer Card. Sales invoices use or can specify the document currency, allowing the invoice to be issued in that foreign currency. Vendor configuration is for purchase transactions, and exchange-rate adjustment revalues posted entries rather than setting up invoice currency.

**Learn more:** [Currencies in Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-currencies) · [Set up currencies in Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-set-up-currencies)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],To satisfy the Commission requirements, you must enforce restrictions on which salespeople can be paired with which regions.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Set Salesperson and Region dimensions to Limited.
Assign Default Dimension Priorities to list Salesperson first.
Set the dimension combination between the Salesperson and the Region to Blocked.
Add Default Dimensions for Salesperson on Customer Cards.

questions.explanation: In Business Central, dimension combination rules (Finance > Dimensions > Dimension Combinations) let you define, for a pair of dimensions such as Salesperson and Region, whether specific value combinations are allowed, generate a warning, or are Blocked. Setting the combination between the Salesperson and Region dimensions to Blocked is the mechanism that actually enforces which salesperson/region pairings are disallowed, which is required to meet the Commission restriction requirement. Setting a dimension to Limited only restricts the individual values allowed for that single dimension; it does not restrict combinations between two dimensions. Default Dimension Priorities only govern which value is used by default when a conflict exists, and adding default dimensions on customer cards merely supplies default values — neither enforces a restriction on valid combinations.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has used Dynamics 365 Business Central for many years.  
  
A new accounting manager reviews the company’s chart of accounts and wants to remove certain general ledger accounts.  
  
The **Check G/L Account Usage** field is selected in **General Ledger Setup**.  
  
You need to help with deleting the accounts.  
  
What is one requirement that allows a general ledger account to be deleted?

options.text: The account cannot be used in any account schedule.
The account cannot be used in any posting groups or posting setup.
The general ledger account is configured to allow for deletion.
The account must have ledger entries.

questions.explanation:
When **Check G/L Account Usage** is selected in General Ledger Setup, a general ledger account must not be used in any posting groups or posting setup before Business Central allows its deletion.

**Learn more:** [Set up or change the chart of accounts - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-setup-chart-accounts)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central. The finance manager creates a new general ledger (G/L) account.  
  
You need to configure the system so that the G/L account is included in the general journal reconciliation window.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add this G/L account to the Bank Account Posting Group.
Enable the Direct Posting field in the G/L account card.
Enable the Reconciliation Account field in the G/L account card.
Create a new payment reconciliation journal.

questions.explanation:
Each G/L account card has a "Reconciliation Account" toggle, and enabling it includes that account in the Reconciliation window that you can open from a general journal (Process > Reconcile). This lets you preview the net change effect on the account before the journal is posted. Enabling Direct Posting (B) only controls whether the account can be posted to directly, adding it to a Bank Account Posting Group (A) relates to bank accounts, and creating a payment reconciliation journal (D) is a different feature for matching bank payments. Therefore you enable the Reconciliation Account field on the G/L account card.

**Learn more:** [Reconciliation with the general ledger](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/design-details-reconciliation-with-the-general-ledger)

questions.question:
A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
Which field is used to calculate the Due Date from the Payment Terms?
questions.explanation:
Business Central uses the **Document Date** on sales and purchase documents as the basis for calculating payment due dates from the assigned payment terms; the Posting Date is not used for this calculation.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set up payment terms - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/dynamics365/business-central/finance-payment-terms)

questions.question:
A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
The company needs to control the periods during which users can post deferrals in the system.  
  
You need to configure the system.  
  
From which page should you configure the system?
questions.explanation:
The User Setup page provides the user-specific **Allow Deferral Posting From** and **Allow Deferral Posting To** fields, which define the date range in which a user may post deferrals.\
\
**Learn more:** [Defer revenues and expenses - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-how-defer-revenue-expenses)

questions.question:
A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
The company needs to control the periods during which users can post deferrals in the system.  
  
You need to configure the system.  
  
From which page should you configure the system?
questions.explanation:
The **Direct Posting** setting on a G/L account enables direct entries to that account from general journals. Account Category and Income/Balance are classification fields, and Default Deferral Template controls deferral behavior rather than posting permission.

**Learn more:** [Table "G/L Account"](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/application/base-application/table/microsoft.finance.generalledger.account.g-l-account) · [Post transactions directly to the general ledger](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-how-post-transactions-directly)

questions.question:
Solution: Use RapidStart Services to import the data.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
In this repeated-scenario item the goal is to transfer opening balances (and master data) into Business Central. Simply importing raw comma-separated values (CSV) files is not a supported migration path, so the solution does NOT meet the goal. Business Central's native tooling loads and validates data through configuration packages / RapidStart and the data migration assisted setup, which exchange data via Excel (.xlsx) worksheets, not CSV. Because the data must be mapped and validated against 27 defined tables before it is applied, a plain CSV import cannot accomplish the objective. Therefore the answer is No.

**Learn more:** [Use Excel to import data](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/across-import-data-configuration-packages) · [Migrate on-premises data to Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/administration/migrate-data)

Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Opening balances are added by creating and posting journal lines for G/L accounts, customers, vendors, or items after the relevant master data is in place. The Data migration assisted setup wizard alone does not transfer and post the required opening-balance entries.\

questions.question:

questions.question:

\

questions.question:
A company is based in India and purchases materials from Sweden.  
  
You need to configure invoice discount terms for a vendor located in Sweden.  
  
Which three items should you enter? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Vendor invoice discount terms specify the applicable currency, the minimum invoice amount that qualifies for the discount, and the discount percentage. Minimum quantity and starting date are criteria for purchase price or line-discount agreements, not invoice discount terms.\
\
**Learn more:** [Record special purchase prices and discounts - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/dynamics365/business-central/purchasing-how-record-purchase-price-discount-payment-agreements)

In **Approval User Setup**, you configure the following users:

You create and enable an approval workflow, configuring it to use the **Approver Chain** approver limit type.  
  
To test the workflow, User1 creates a purchase order for $1,100 and uses **Send Approval Request**.  
  
You need to determine which actions occur when the workflow runs.  
  
Which set of actions occurs?

options.text: User4 will receive an approval request. Once approved, the purchase order is released.
User3 receives an approval request. Once User3 approves the request, the purchase order is released.
User2 will receive an approval request. Once User2 approves the request, User3 will receive an approval request. Once User2 and User3 approve the request, the purchase order is released.

questions.explanation:

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are implementing Dynamics 365 Business Central for a company. The accounting manager gives you the chart of accounts, and you are configuring posting groups for the accounting department.  
  
You must use a standard costing method and post differences between actual purchase costs and the standard cost.  
  
You need to configure a general ledger account to post any cost differences.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are configuring a new company for a customer.  
  
The customer wants to sell items in boxes and pallets, while referring to the items as pieces. Each box contains 12 pieces. Each pallet contains 144 pieces.  
  
You need to assign units of measure to the items.  
  
How should you assign the units of measure?

options.text: Create Box as a base unit of measure. Add Pieces as an item unit of measure with the quantity per unit set to 0.08333.
Create Pieces as an item unit of measure with a quantity per unit of measure set to 1.
Create Pieces as a base unit of measure. Add Box as an item unit of measure with the quantity per unit set to 12.
Create Pallet as a base unit of measure. Add Box as an item unit of measure with the quantity per unit set to 0.08333.

questions.explanation:
The base unit of measure is the inventory and conversion basis and must have a quantity per unit of measure of 1. An alternate item unit records the number of base units it contains. Therefore, Pieces is the base unit, and Box is an alternate unit with a quantity per unit of 12.

**Learn more:** [Set up item units of measure - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/inventory-how-setup-units-of-measure)

questions.explanation:

You need to configure the system to satisfy this requirement.

questions.question:

Assign the payment terms to the customer price group.
Assign the payment terms to the customer.

The company made an error on a posted sales invoice and needs to correct it.  
  
You need to verify whether the posted sales invoice can be corrected or whether a new corrective credit memo must be created.  
  
Which validation action should you perform?

The general ledger account is configured to allow for deletion

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company deploys Dynamics 365 Business Central.

You need to configure sales and receivables.  
  
Which two settings should you configure? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
The **Shipment on Invoice** setting automatically creates a posted shipment and a posted invoice when an invoice is posted. The **Return Receipt on Credit Memo** setting automatically creates a posted return receipt and a posted sales credit memo when a credit memo is posted. These settings post the associated inventory documents together with their respective sales transactions.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
A vendor supplies items within one week after the company places an order. The vendor ships the items by train.  
  
You need to configure the vendor card.
questions.explanation:
Lead Time Calculation records the vendor lead time used to calculate planned receipt and order dates; it should therefore represent the one-week interval. Shipment Method Code records the desired delivery method on vendor cards and should represent shipment by train. A base calendar affects working-day date calculations, while a location code does not define either the vendor’s lead time or transport method.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A customer uses Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
The customer currently sends quotes and invoices through postal services and wants to start emailing quotes and invoices directly from Business Central.  
  
You need to configure outbound email.  
  
What are two possible ways to accomplish this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Run the Set up your Business Inbox in Outlook assisted setup tool.
Run the Set up email logging assisted setup tool.
Run the Email setup assisted setup tool.

questions.explanation:
