The Set Up Email assisted setup configures this outbound-email capability, and SMTP configuration provides an SMTP-based outbound mail path. Business Inbox in Outlook and email logging serve Outlook integration and correspondence-recording purposes, respectively, rather than configuring document delivery.

**Learn more:** [Set up email in Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/admin-how-setup-email) · [Send documents and emails](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/dynamics365/business-central/ui-how-send-documents-email)

questions.question:
You are configuring Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
You need to set up the Direct Cost Applied account.  
  
Where should you configure the accounts for Direct Cost Applied?
questions.explanation:
The **Direct Cost Applied Account** is configured in **General Posting Setup**. Business Central selects it through the applicable General Business Posting Group and General Product Posting Group for the posting transaction.\
\
**Learn more:** [Design details: Accounts in the general ledger — Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/uk-ua/dynamics365/business-central/design-details-accounts-in-the-general-ledger)

questions.question:
You are configuring Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
You need to set up the Direct Cost Applied account.  
  
Where should you configure the accounts for Direct Cost Applied?

options.text: On the Sales & Receivables Setup page, select Invoice Discount in Discount Posting.
On the Sales & Receivables Setup page, select Calc. Inv. Discount.
On the Customer card, select Invoice Disc. Code.
On the Sales & Receivables Setup page, select Lowest Price in Price Calculation Method.

questions.explanation:
Selecting **Calc. Inv. Discount** on the Sales & Receivables Setup page causes Business Central to automatically calculate invoice discount amounts for sales documents, using eligible sales lines and the applicable customer invoice-discount terms.

**Learn more:** [Record special sales prices and discounts - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/dynamics365/business-central/sales-how-record-sales-price-discount-payment-agreements) · [Sales & Receivables Setup table - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/application/base-application/table/microsoft.sales.setup.sales-%26-receivables-setup)

questions.question:
A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
The company needs to control the periods in which users can post deferrals in the system.  
  
You need to configure the system.  
  
From which page should you perform the configuration?
questions.explanation:
Business Central configures user-specific deferral-posting periods on the User Setup page by using the Allow Deferral Posting From and Allow Deferral Posting To fields.\
\
**Learn more:** [Defer revenues and expenses - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-how-defer-revenue-expenses)

questions.question:
A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
The company needs to control the periods in which users can post deferrals in the system.  
  
You need to configure the system.  
  
From which page should you perform the configuration?

options.text: Create Box as a base unit of measure. Add Pallet as an item unit of measure with the quantity per unit set to 12.
Create Pieces as an item unit of measure with a quantity per unit of measure set to 1.
Create Pieces as a base unit of measure. Add Box as an item unit of measure with the quantity per unit set to 12.
Create Boxes as an item unit of measure with a quantity per unit of measure set to 1.

questions.explanation: The base unit of measure should be Pieces because it is the individual unit from which the larger packaging units are derived. Box should be an item unit of measure with a quantity per unit of 12; Pallet can similarly be configured with a quantity per unit of 144.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are deploying Dynamics 365 Business Central for a customer.  
  
The customer needs to manually add many similar items. You must help the customer make copies of existing items.  
  
Which three actions must be completed? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: On the Set up Customer/Vendor/Item Templates page, create a new item template
Open an existing item, and then click the Save as Template action on the item card
On the Set Up Customer/Vendor/Item Templates page, edit the information in the newly created item template
On the Configuration Templates page, create a new template for item table
Create a new item, and then select the new template name to copy the information to the item

questions.explanation:
An existing Item Card can be saved as an item template by using the **Save as Template** action. The resulting item template can be edited to set the values that new item cards will inherit. When a new item is created, selecting that template populates the new item with the template information. Microsoft Learn documents this item-template workflow.

**Learn more:** [Create item cards for goods or services - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/inventory-how-register-new-items)

questions.question:
A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central. All system activity is in the company's local currency.  
  
Sales invoice amounts must be rounded to the nearest interval according to the amount.  
  
You need to finish the configuration. Where should you configure the setup?
questions.explanation:
For local-currency invoice rounding, Business Central uses the **Inv. Rounding Precision** and **Inv. Rounding Type** fields on the **General Ledger Setup** page. Setting the rounding type to Nearest and specifying the precision defines the required interval. Sales & Receivables Setup only activates the sales invoice-rounding feature.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set up invoice rounding - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/dynamics365/business-central/finance-set-up-invoice-rounding)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company located in the United States uses Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
A customer agrees to purchase raw materials in MXN (Mexican Peso).  
  
You need to configure the currency and exchange rates for this purchase.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Do not configure the currency MXN and recalculate all entries in USD before posting.
Configure the currency MXN, then set up the Currency Exchange Rate Service to upload currency rates automatically.
Use the currency MXN as a local currency in the system, then set the exchange rates manually before posting.
Use the currency MXN as an additional reporting currency, then set up the Currency Exchange Rate Service to upload rates automatically.

questions.explanation:
Business Central requires a currency code for transactions conducted in currencies other than the local currency, and it converts foreign-currency postings to the local currency using the exchange rate applicable on the posting date. A Currency Exchange Rate Service can retrieve and update those foreign-currency rates automatically. An additional reporting currency is intended for parallel financial reporting, not for setting up an ordinary MXN transaction currency.

**Learn more:** [Set up currencies - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-set-up-currencies) · [Update currency exchange rates - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/dynamics365/business-central/finance-how-update-currencies)

questions.question:
Solution: On the Report Selection - Service page, set the **Usage** option to **Order**. Change the **Report ID** displayed on the page to the new report object.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Purchase orders must be configured on the **Report Selection - Purchase** page. An **Order** usage on **Report Selection - Service** applies to service orders, so changing its Report ID cannot set the system-default report for printed purchase orders. Microsoft documents that report-selection pages configure default reports by document type and identifies separate Purchase and Service report-selection pages.\
\
**Learn more:** [Report selection for documents in Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/across-report-selections)

questions.question:
Solution: On the Report Selection - Purchase page, set the Usage option to **Order**. Update the Report ID displayed on the page to match the new report object.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Business Central uses the Report Selection - Purchase setup to assign default reports for purchase document types. The **Order** usage applies to purchase orders, so setting that row’s Report ID to the deployed custom report makes it the system default when purchase orders are printed.\
\
**Learn more:** [Report selection for documents in Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/across-report-selections) · [Enum \"Report Selection Usage Purchase\"](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/application/base-application/enum/microsoft.purchases.setup.report-selection-usage-purchase)

questions.question:
Solution: On the **Custom Report Layouts** page, choose the new report object. Use the **Update Layout** function to make Business Central use the current report design.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
The **Update Layout** action updates a custom report layout when the report dataset or design has changed; it does not set a report object as the default report for purchase orders. Default purchase-document reports are configured through the **Report Selections - Purchase** page, where the report used for the relevant document usage is selected.\
\
**Learn more:** [Report selection for documents in Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/across-report-selections) · [Update Custom Report Layouts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/dynamics365/business-central/ui-update-report-layouts)

questions.question:
Solution: On the **Report Layout Selection** page, choose the new report object. Change the value to **Custom Layout** and select the updated layout.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Report Layout Selection page sets the layout used by an individual report, whereas the Report Selection - Purchase page determines which report object is used when purchase documents such as purchase orders are printed. Selecting a custom layout for the new report does not replace the purchase-order report selection with that report object.\
\
**Learn more:** [Report selection for documents in Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/across-report-selections) · [Set the layout used by a report](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/dynamics365/business-central/ui-set-report-layout)

questions.question:
Solution: On the **Report Layout Selection** page, choose the new report object. Change the value to **Custom Layout** and select the updated layout.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Locations represent the warehouses and provide the location codes used to associate inventory transactions with a specific location. An item card defines the base item record. Stockkeeping units are item-and-location records and can hold location-specific information such as vendor, direct cost, replenishment settings, and related inventory parameters, allowing the same item to be configured differently at each warehouse.

**Learn more:** [Set up stockkeeping units — Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/inventory-how-to-set-up-stockkeeping-units) · [Stockkeeping Unit table — Business Central application](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/application/base-application/table/microsoft.inventory.location.stockkeeping-unit)

questions.question:
A company purchases items using cash. A vendor payment is registered when a purchase invoice for a cash vendor is posted.  
  
You are creating a new cash vendor, and no vendors have previously been configured as cash vendors.  
  
You need to configure the vendor so that payments are posted automatically when a purchase invoice is posted.  
  
Which type of setup should you use?

options.text: Payment Method as Cash with balancing account

questions.explanation:
A payment method configured with a balancing account supplies the cash or bank balancing account on each new purchase invoice for that vendor. When the invoice is posted, Business Central can post and apply the corresponding vendor payment automatically.\
\
**Learn more:** [Settle purchase invoices promptly - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-how-to-settle-purchase-invoices-promptly)

questions.question:
A company records item descriptions by vendor.  
  
You need to configure vendor-specific descriptions for items.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Item cross-references, now termed item references in Business Central, associate an item with a vendor’s item information. They can store the vendor’s item description and insert it on relevant purchase documents.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use item references - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-au/dynamics365/business-central/inventory-how-use-item-cross-refs)

questions.question:
A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
The company conducts an annual review of customer prices and decides that sales prices must increase by 10% for the upcoming year.  
  
You need to update the prices.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use the action Suggest Item Price on Worksheet.
Implement price changes to the sales price worksheet.
Manually add new lines to the Sales Lines Discount page.

questions.explanation:
The **Suggest Item Price on Wksh.** batch job bulk-generates updated item sales-price suggestions and supports an Adjustment Factor. An adjustment factor of 1.10 produces a 10% price increase; the resulting worksheet lines can subsequently be implemented as price changes.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set up prices and discounts - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/dynamics365/business-central/across-prices-and-discounts)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to configure the process for creating new customers.  
  
Which two areas must you configure? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Configuration templates standardize the default values applied when a new customer record is created, while permissions authorize the users who create or maintain customer records. Responsibility centers are used to scope business documents and operations, and configuration worksheets support company setup and configuration packages rather than routine customer creation.

**Learn more:** [Register new customers by creating a Customer Card - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/sales-how-register-new-customers) · [Assign permissions to users and groups - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/ui-define-granular-permissions)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Two cash receipts have been applied to a posted sales transaction. The first receipt was applied by mistake.  
  
You need to remove the first cash receipt from the posted sales transaction.  
  
Which sequence of steps should you take?

options.text: 1. Navigate to Unapply Entries from the relevant customer ledger entry. 2. Unapply the second payment. 3. Unapply the first payment. 4. Apply the second payment to the customer ledger entry.

1. Navigate to Reverse Transaction from the relevant detailed customer ledger entry. 2. Reverse the second payment. 3. Reverse the first payment. 4. Apply the second payment to the customer ledger entry.
1. Navigate to Reverse Transaction from the relevant customer ledger entry. 2. Reverse the second payment. 3. Reverse the first payment. 4. Apply the second payment to the customer ledger entry.
1. Post a reversing Cash Receipt and select the customer and relevant payment entry. 2. Navigate to Unapply Entries from the relevant customer ledger entry. 3. Unapply the payment.

questions.explanation:
Business Central requires applications to be unapplied in reverse chronological order when more than one application entry exists. Unapplying the second receipt first allows the first, erroneous receipt to be unapplied; the valid second receipt can then be applied again to the customer ledger entry. [Reconcile customer payments with the cash receipt journal or from customer ledger entries](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/receivables-how-apply-sales-transactions-manually)

**Learn more:** [Reconcile customer payments with the cash receipt journal or from customer ledger entries](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/receivables-how-apply-sales-transactions-manually)

questions.question:
You have configured a cloud-based printer in Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
Purchase orders printed by users must be automatically sent to the cloud-based printer.  
  
You need to create a setup record for the user, report, and printer combination.  
  
On which page should you create this setup record?
questions.explanation:
The **Printer Selections** page creates printer-selection records. A record containing a User ID, Report ID, and Printer Name assigns a specific report to a specific printer for a specific user, so it can automatically route purchase-order printing to the configured cloud printer.\
\
**Learn more:** [Specify a default printer - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/ui-specify-printer-selection-reports)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A production company is deploying Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
The company must be able to analyze the total acquisition and maintenance costs for each production line.  
  
Production lines must be configured as main assets, with every machine on a line configured as a component. Only the machines on the production line must have a book value and be depreciated.  
  
You need to configure the system so that postings for the production-line assets are correct.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer is part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Make the production line asset inactive.
Open the fixed asset card for the production line.
Open the Fixed Asset Setup page.

questions.explanation:
A main asset can group component fixed assets, and the main asset’s Fixed Asset Card is where its component list is maintained. Disabling posting to main assets ensures that acquisition and depreciation postings are made only to the component machines, so the production-line grouping asset does not obtain a book value or depreciation.

**Learn more:** [Acquire fixed assets - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/fa-how-acquire)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Dynamics 265 Business Central.  
  
The company intends to use multiple unit prices for the same items from different vendors.  
  
You need to configure the items’ purchase prices.  
  
In which two locations can you configure the purchase prices? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Business Central purchase prices are configured as vendor-and-item price agreements. A special purchase price can be entered from the relevant vendor card by using the **Prices** action, and the same configuration can be entered from the item card because purchase prices are based on the item-vendor combination.

**Learn more:** [Record special purchase prices and discounts - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/purchasing-how-record-purchase-price-discount-payment-agreements)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is implementing Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
You need to create a new payment terms record that meets these requirements:  
  
- Ensure the due date for every vendor invoice is 30 days.  
- Give vendors a two percent discount when an invoice is paid within 10 days.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Set the value of the Discount Date Calculation field to 2D.
Set the value of the Discount Date Calculation field to 10D.
Set the value of the Discount % field to 2.
Set the value of the Due Date Calculation field to 30D.
Set the value of the Discount % field to 10.

questions.explanation:
In Business Central payment terms, **Due Date Calculation** defines when payment is due, **Discount Date Calculation** defines the deadline for qualifying for a payment discount, and **Discount %** defines that discount rate. The required values are therefore `30D`, `10D`, and `2`, respectively. [Set Up Payment Terms (Business Central)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/localfunctionality/italy/how-to-set-up-payment-terms)

**Learn more:** [Set Up Payment Terms (Business Central)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/localfunctionality/italy/how-to-set-up-payment-terms)

questions.question:
Solution: Open the fixed asset G/L journal. Enter the machine's fixed asset number and select **Acquisition Cost** as the fixed asset posting type. Enter the installation and delivery fee in the **Amount** field, then insert the fixed asset balance account. Post the journal.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A Fixed Asset G/L Journal can post an Acquisition Cost entry to an existing fixed asset against the appropriate balancing G/L account. The posted installation and delivery amount increases the machine’s acquisition cost, allowing that capitalized total to be depreciated over the asset’s useful life.\
\
**Learn more:** [Acquire fixed assets - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/fa-how-acquire)

questions.question:
Solution: Open the fixed asset G/L journal. Enter the machine's fixed asset number and select **Appreciation** as the fixed asset posting type. Enter the combined installation and delivery fees in the **Amount** field. Add the fixed asset balance account and post the journal.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Capitalizable installation and delivery fees related to acquiring a machine must be posted as **Acquisition Cost** in the Fixed Asset G/L Journal. **Appreciation** is used for a revaluation increase in an asset’s value, not for additional purchase-related acquisition costs.\
\
**Learn more:** [Acquire fixed assets - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/fa-how-acquire) · [Revalue fixed assets - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/fa-how-revalue)

questions.question:
Solution: Use the **Cancel Fixed Asset Entries** batch job to cancel the acquisition-cost posting for the machine. Post a corrected acquisition entry with the total acquisition cost of the machine, installation, and delivery.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Business Central lets you cancel an incorrect fixed-asset acquisition posting with the Cancel FA Entries batch job and post a corrected acquisition entry. Posting the combined machine, installation, and delivery amounts as the acquisition cost capitalizes the total cost on the fixed asset, making it available for depreciation over its useful life.\
\
**Learn more:** [Acquire fixed assets - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/fa-how-acquire)

questions.question:
Solution: Create a purchase invoice for the installation and delivery fees. Enter the machine's fixed asset number on the invoice lines, then post the invoice.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A purchase invoice line with the type **Fixed Asset** and the existing machine’s fixed asset number posts the invoice amount as an additional acquisition cost of that asset. The added cost is therefore capitalized in the fixed asset value and included in depreciation over the asset’s useful life.\
\
**Learn more:** [Acquire fixed assets - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/fa-how-acquire)

questions.question:
A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
A user posts a Sales Invoice document with an incorrect dimension value.  
  
You need to update the general ledger entries to the correct dimension value without creating new ledger entries.  
  
Which option should you use?
questions.explanation:
The Correct Dimensions action corrects dimension values on posted general ledger entries without creating new G/L entries. It is intended to make financial reporting accurate after an incorrect dimension has been posted.\
\
**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot and correct dimensions - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-troubleshooting-correcting-dimensions)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
A finance manager must import a bank-statement CSV file into Dynamics 365 Business Central.  
  
You need to configure the system for this file import.  
  
Which three pages should you use to complete the configuration? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
A bank-statement CSV import is configured through a Data Exchange Definition that specifies the external file structure and field mappings, a Bank Export/Import Setup that defines the import format and links to that data-exchange definition, and the Bank Account Card, where import/export settings are assigned for the applicable bank account. The Payment Reconciliation Journal is used to import and reconcile statements after the configuration is in place.

**Learn more:** [Set up bank accounts - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/dynamics365/business-central/bank-how-setup-bank-accounts) · [Set up data exchange definitions - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/across-how-to-set-up-data-exchange-definitions)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Dynamics 365 Business Central to record vendor payments. All payment records contain similar data elements.  
  
You are onboarding a new vendor. You must create a unique number series for payments from that vendor. No other vendors will use the new number series.  
  
You need to configure the system.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
A General Journal template defines the shared structure and default settings for its journal batches, including the **No. Series** used to assign document numbers. A dedicated template can therefore assign a number series that is used only for the new vendor’s payment records. Payment journals are specialized general journals for vendor payments, but the template contains the default number-series configuration.

**Learn more:** [Gen. Journal Template table — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/application/base-application/table/microsoft.finance.generalledger.journal.gen.-journal-template) · [Create number series — Business Central | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/ui-create-number-series)

You are deploying Dynamics 365 Business Central Online for a company that is migrating from an earlier version of Business Central.  
  
The company wants to move historical financial data from the prior fiscal year into the new database, including all analytical information.  
  
You need to migrate the data, including analytical information, by using a configuration package.  
  
Which three steps should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Create a configuration package. Then select the appropriate table.
Export the table from the configuration package to Microsoft Excel. Adjust the file to include dimension information. Import the updated Excel table.

Assign a data template to the configuration package.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to configure workflows to satisfy the company's order-processing requirements.  
  
Which two solutions should you use? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create a purchase order approval workflow.
Use Business Central as the engine for the workflow.
Use Power Automate as the engine for the workflow.
Create a purchase invoice approval workflow.

questions.explanation:
A purchase order approval workflow applies the required approval process to POs. Power Automate supports approval responses from an approver’s email inbox, which satisfies the requirement to approve POs by email without opening Business Central. A purchase invoice approval workflow applies to the wrong document type, and the Business Central approval workflow alone requires users to access Business Central to approve requests.

Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Standard Purchase Code Cards are used for recurring purchase lines and can be assigned to vendors for use on purchase documents. They do not set default general ledger accounts on Customer Cards or automate sales-side monthly subscription invoicing.\
\
**Learn more:** [Standard recurring purchase lines - Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/purchasing-how-work-recurring-purchase-lines)

questions.question:
Solution: Set up a Document Layout on the Customer Card.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Customer document layouts define the appearance and delivery settings of sales documents, including report layouts and recipient email addresses. They do not assign general ledger accounts; G/L-account mapping is configured through posting groups and General Posting Setup.\
\
**Learn more:** [Define document layouts for customers and vendors](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-au/dynamics365/business-central/ui-define-customer-vendor-document-layouts) · [Understand the general ledger and Chart of Accounts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-general-ledger)

questions.question:

Does the solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:

\

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are configuring a new company for a customer.  
  
The customer wants to sell items in boxes and pallets, while referring to the items as pieces. Each box contains 12 pieces. Each pallet contains 144 pieces.  
  
You need to assign units of measure to the items.  
  
How should you assign the units of measure?

options.text: Create Boxes as an item unit of measure with a quantity per unit of measure set to 1.
Create Pieces as a base unit of measure. Add Box as an item unit of measure with the quantity per unit set to 12.
Create Pallet as a base unit of measure. Add Pieces as an item unit of measure with the quantity per unit set to 0.0069.
Create Box as a base unit of measure. Add Pallet as an item unit of measure with the quantity per unit set to 12.

questions.explanation:
In Business Central, the base unit of measure is the unit in which inventory is stored, and an alternate item's **Qty. per Unit of Measure** specifies how many base units it contains. Pieces should therefore be the base unit, and Box should be an alternate unit with a quantity per unit of 12.
